### 1. What the caller expresses, and what the simulator does

- **Target object.** Clearly expressed. The caller gives `M-55012` unprompted ("he offers his membership number, M-55012, early on"). Asked which account, he says "it is the big tank at the dryer and not the little one up at the house, and that the dryer tank is the one he pre-buys gallons on every spring". `find_energy_accounts` returns exactly two open accounts: `EA-551204` (Contract Gallon Pre-Buy Account, propane, 1000 gal tank, `contract_gallons` 2400, `current_gallons_owed` 1300) and `EA-551188` (Will-Call Propane Account, propane, 500 gal tank, `contract_gallons` 0). The larger tank + the pre-buy both point at `EA-551204`; the object is unique.
- **Timing.** "he wants to pay it off today, in full, before the corn comes off". Act now.
- **Boundary of the action.** "He is not after a payment arrangement and not after a part payment: he wants the one figure that clears the account outright, today, and he will say so plainly if the agent offers him anything less than that."
- **Mode of authorisation.** "He is content for the agent to act for him on the account, and says as much if the agent asks whether it is all right to work on it". The money itself he moves himself: "The money he will move himself, from the farm's own bank account, as a transfer. He will not read card numbers down a telephone and he is not going to put a cheque in the post."
- **Simulator behaviour.** Passive and if/else only: it conveys the need, answers identity questions when asked (`M-55012`; then `5512`; then `5150550142`), refuses to guess the balance, and executes the user-owned tool only when handed over ("When the agent has the figure worked out and hands the payment over for him to make, he makes it there and then"). "If the agent quotes him a figure without ever putting anything through, he just waits to be told how to send it." It never pushes the procedure along.
- Identity: `verify_member_identity` states "identity clears only when at least two of them agree with what is on file. The membership reference is used only to pull the right profile up and never counts as one of those matching details". The profile returns `tax_id_last4: '5512'` and `phone_number: '5150550142'`; both are offered on request, so K=2 is reachable.

Tier evidence, query return by query return:
- *Held back.* `keep_full_enrolled: True` → "The tank stands on the automatic keep-full schedule". Stops in the twelve months ending 2026-09-14: 2025-11-12, 2026-02-03, 2026-06-09, 2026-07-08, 2026-08-22, 2026-09-02 = **6 ≥ 3** → first line: "the programme's fill-to percentage of the tank's water capacity less the gauge reading the driver recorded at the most recent stop". Most recent stop 2026-09-02 carries `tank_percent_before: 44.0`, `tank_percent_after: 74.0`. The document's own illustration fixes which reading is meant — "The driver's gauge reading at the most recent stop was 35 percent. The held-back gallons are 80 percent less 35 percent of 1000.0 gallons, coming to 450.0 gallons": a reading below the fill-to, i.e. the reading found on arrival. (Reading it as the after-fill figure would make the rule degenerate — a keep-full fill always ends at the fill-to, so the held-back figure would be 0 by construction.) So (80 − 44) % × 1000 = **360.0**.
- *Rack of record.* Called-in (`will_call`) stops billed in the three months ending 2026-09-14: 2026-07-08 @ 1.21 and 2026-09-02 @ 1.19 = **2**, so line 1 "2 or more": average = 1.2000, less the margin 0.8000.
- *Margin allowed.* Gallons taken in the twelve months = 520+470+620+350+480+300 = **2740.0 ≥ 1800**; gallons drawn against bookings = **1100.0 ≥ 1000** → both tests of line 1 → margin reduced by 0.06.
- *Protected floor.* `find_grain_ledger_entries` → three `grain_delivery_applied` rows in the window, net bushels 15420.5 + 16880.25 + 14519.25 = **46820.0 ≥ 40000**; gallons booked 2400.0 ≥ 1000 → line 1, floor 90 + 3.0 = 93.0 %, "taken on the price the gallons were booked at" = 1.49.
- *Protection already credited.* **2** `energy_price_protection_credited` rows in the twelve months (2026-06-30, 2026-07-31); gallons booked 2400.0 ≥ twice the minimum pre-buy gallons (2 × 1000 = 2000) → line 1, "the whole of the protection already credited in that window".

3. `find_energy_accounts {customer_id}` → the two accounts; `find_energy_deliveries {energy_account_id: "c2cc7c02-…"}`; `find_grain_ledger_entries {customer_id}`.

Owner **agent** — E.7: "which the agent unlocks and then calls".
5. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` + `call_agent_discoverable_tool` **`bill_budget_plan_reconciliation_cfd56d13`** — `energy_account_id` `c2cc7c02-…`, `reconciliation_amount_usd` `719.61`. Owner **agent** — E.9: "which the agent unlocks and then calls".
6. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` **`post_energy_account_clearing_payment_6fe49ac6`**, handed to the member, who calls it: `energy_account_id` `c2cc7c02-…`, `invoice_number` `EI-440712`, `payment_reference` `EP-118692`, `payment_method` `ach`, `payment_amount_usd` `3724.08`. Owner **user** — E.12: "It is the member's own money and the member's own act, so the desk unlocks the tool and hands it over for the customer themselves to run; the desk does not run it for them."

`invoice_number`: E.12 fixes it as "the one standing unpaid on the account with the earliest date on it". The invoices with no matching `energy_payment_posted` row are EI-440629, EI-440632, EI-440712, EI-440788, EI-440841, EI-440866, EI-440902, EI-440931; the earliest-dated of these is **EI-440712** (2025-11-12).

Forward dependency: 4 and 5 must both precede 6, because the amount paid at 6 is assembled from lines that 4 and 5 write. 4 and 5 are independent of each other (a credit allowed does not enter the year's cost or the plan's collection; the true-up does not enter the protection credit). Backward: nothing after 6.

Terminal state: the account carries a protection credit line dated 2026-09, a true-up line among the instalments, and a payment of 3724.08 applied to EI-440712; the balance owed falls to nothing. The account remains `active` — the member asked to clear it, not to close it, and E.24's closure is not triggered by anything he says.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, in handling order.**

| # | Problem | Depends on | Hop mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Record the downside protection credit on booking EC-330742 (E.7) | — | root of its branch |
| P2 | Bill the level plan true-up for the plan year just past (E.9) | — | root of its branch |
| P3 | Take the payment that clears the account (E.12) — the only thing the customer asked for | P1, P2 | **state-derived** (both edges) |

**Hop P3 → P1, reasoning chain.**
1. The customer's request is governed by E.12 (`paying_an_energy_account_clear_6dcdca30`), whose own rule says: *"The amount that clears the account is fixed only after the account carries, on every pre-buy booking whose protected floor stood above the posted price, a downside protection credit dated in the month the amount is worked out."* This names a **state of the record** ("the account carries … a downside protection credit dated in …"), with the ordering connective "only after". It names no tool, no other document and no performer.
2. Does the state hold? `find_energy_accounts` shows one pre-buy position (`contract_gallons: 2400`, `current_gallons_owed: 1300`); `find_energy_deliveries` shows one booking, `EC-330742`. The protected floor on it is 1.3857 (93.0 % of the booked 1.49) and the posted price is 1.1400 — the floor stands above the posted price, so the booking is one the sentence speaks of. The only `energy_price_protection_credited` rows on the account are dated **2026-06-30** and **2026-07-31**; the amount is being worked out in **2026-09**. **The state does not hold.**
3. Which write brings it about? Searching the corpus in the words the sentence and the records use for that state — "downside protection credit", "protection credited", "credit … on a pre-buy booking" — reaches E.7, `crediting_downside_protection_to_a_members_account_561fb402`: *"Where downside protection sold with a pre-buy booking held on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts falls to be credited, the desk works the money out and records it against that booking… it is dated the day the desk works it out"*. That is the write that puts a protection credit dated today onto the account. E.12 nowhere names E.7, its tool or its policy; the hop is worked out from the two rules plus the ledger. → **state-derived**.

**Hop P3 → P2, reasoning chain.**
1. E.12 also says: *"Before the amount that clears the account is worked out, the account must carry the true-up entry owed for every budget plan year that has passed its reconciliation date."* Again a state of the record, with the ordering connective "before".
2. Does it hold? `find_energy_accounts` shows `budget_monthly_amount: 385.0`, and the ledger carries eleven `energy_budget_installment_billed` rows for billing months 2025-08 … 2026-06 — a level plan on the account. `level_payment_plan_settings_by_programme_b8a56b3f` writes for the Contract Gallon Pre-Buy Account: plan carried, 11 instalments, plan year begins 1 August, **trued up on 15 July**. The plan year that began 1 August 2025 ran its eleven instalments and its reconciliation date, 15 July 2026, has passed on the handling date 2026-09-14. The ledger carries **no** true-up entry of any kind. **The state does not hold.**
3. Which write brings it about? Searching in the sentence's and the record's own words — "true-up", "budget plan year", "reconciliation" — reaches E.9, `billing_the_budget_plan_true_up_e01f5931`: *"At the close of a plan year on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts the desk settles the level plan against what the member actually used and puts the result onto the account as a single true-up line among the instalments billed there."* → **state-derived**.

**No further hops.** E.7's own document carries no prerequisite sentence; E.9's own document carries none. Both are leaves, and the tree closes at depth 1.

**Pre-solving check.** Neither E.12 sentence names a tool, a policy id, another document, a performer or a route, and neither E.7 nor E.9 says who is waiting on it. No document anywhere in the 71 strings the three problems into a procedure. No hop is marked pre-solved.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure above is read from a published document plus a tool return; none needed an outside source.

**Closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

| Alternative | Excluded by |
| --- | --- |
| Pay the *other* account, or spread the money | `credit_and_contracted_gallons_across_a_members_accounts_ce870877`: "A payment that names no invoice is applied to the account it was received on, oldest invoice first, and is never spread across accounts." EA-551188 carries `account_balance: 0.0` besides. |
| Use the account's `account_balance` 3053.95 as the figure | The *Energy Arrears Working Basis* defines the amount that clears as "the amount standing plus the late charge plus the service charge less the settlement allowance"; the balance is only the first term. |
| Take the closing-settlement assembly (which adds the money committed on bookings and subtracts the money applied against them) | `the_balance_an_energy_account_closes_at_23aeab46` is written for "the balance an account … closes at", and the member asks to pay, not to close. The arrears basis names its own quantities: "the fuel billed, the fees billed and the instalments billed, less the payments posted and the credits allowed". That the arrears assembly reproduces the system's `account_balance` to the cent confirms it is the right one. |
| Start the clock at the invoice date | `energy_invoices_falling_due_and_falling_behind_cd3ebfaf` writes the invoice-date clause as *retired*: "The clause formerly stated here — 'An energy invoice falls due the programme's terms in calendar days after the invoice date…' — is carried for the record and is no longer in force". The arrears basis anchors on "the date of the most recent payment posted on the account". |
| Use the programme's 15.00 late charge | `late_charge_where_the_level_plan_has_lapsed_a0173740` line 2 puts it at 30.00 at 6 draft-months; 15.00 only applies at 11 or more. |
| Round the months to 2 whole thirty-day months | `counting_the_months_deep_arrears_bear_a_charge_for_d05317c9` line 1 gives 2.6333 because days overdue ≥ 60 and 3 stops fall in the quarter. |
| `credit_card` or `check` as the payment method | The persona closes it: "He will not read card numbers down a telephone and he is not going to put a cheque in the post, and he says so if either is suggested." The catalogue leaves all five channels open on this programme, so the **source** leaves this open and the documents rightly do not close it — the persona does. |
| The agent running the payment tool itself | E.12: "the desk unlocks the tool and hands it over for the customer themselves to run; the desk does not run it for them." |

**Openness recorded, not treated as a defect.** Two readings are left genuinely open by the visible corpus and I record them as policy-side notes rather than document defects:
- *(i)* `gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db` says "the gauge reading the driver recorded at the most recent stop"; the delivery row carries **two** driver readings (`tank_percent_before: 44.0`, `tank_percent_after: 74.0`). The document's own worked illustration (a 35 % reading against an 80 % fill-to) and the fact that the "after" reading would make the rule vacuous on a keep-full programme close it in favour of the arrival reading, but the sentence alone does not name which column.
- *(ii)* `what_counts_as_the_plans_collection_4613d0d6` counts "payment[s] reached the cooperative by bank transfer". The ledger's `energy_contract_gallons_booked` row also carries `payment_method: 'ach'` and `payment_reference: 'EP-118440'` for 3576.00. I read the collection's bank transfers as the `energy_payment_posted` rows only (600.00), since the booking row is money "committed on the booking" (E.15) rather than a payment on the account. Either reading puts the account on the same tier; only the summed figure would differ.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — excluding "do only the one thing the customer asked for".**
Suppose the agent takes only a payment. The figure it would take is 3053.95 (or the baseline 3160.57 below). Visible principles then leave the account in a state they do not allow:
- E.12's own rule says the amount "is fixed only after the account carries, on every pre-buy booking whose protected floor stood above the posted price, a downside protection credit dated in the month the amount is worked out". Booking EC-330742's floor (1.3857) stands above its posted price (1.1400) and no credit is dated 2026-09; the amount would therefore not be fixed at all, and the money paid would leave 115.26 of credit unallowed.
- E.12 also says the account "must carry the true-up entry owed for every budget plan year that has passed its reconciliation date". 15 July 2026 has passed and no true-up entry exists; a payment of 3053.95 would leave 719.61 still to be billed, so the account would not be clear — which is exactly what the member asked for ("he wants the one figure that clears the account outright").
Neither exclusion rests on a tool name, a route or an aggregated chain: both rest on E.12's own two sentences read against `find_energy_deliveries` and `level_payment_plan_settings_by_programme_b8a56b3f`.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back number.**
Reading **only** `arriving_at_the_amount_that_clears_an_account_48d31667` plus the catalogue figures it names, with no factor document applied and the two prerequisite writes not made:
- amount standing 3053.95; most recent payment posted 2026-06-12; days overdue 94 − 15 = 79; months = "the whole thirty-day months in the days overdue, a part month not counting" = 2; rate = the programme's monthly service charge 1.5 %; service charge = 3053.95 × 1.5 % × 2 = 91.6185 → 91.62; late charge = the programme's 15.00 (days overdue stand beyond the grace period of 10); settlement allowance = nothing.
- **Fall-back = 3053.95 + 15.00 + 91.62 − 0.00 = 3160.57 USD.** Definite, computable from that one document, and different from 3724.08.

### Verdict: **KB-RUNTIME RED**

**Symptom.** Reading only the published corpus and the records reachable through the finders, the amount that clears the account comes out at **3724.08 USD** and the protection credit at **115.26 USD on 940.0 gallons**; the scored solution is **3648.14 USD** and **188.97 USD on 1240.0 gallons**. Two of the three scored values in this task are missed, and the third (719.61) is hit exactly.

**Root cause.** The single input that diverges is the gauge reading in the first tier of the hold-back ladder. `energy_deliveries` records **two** driver-recorded gauge readings for every stop — the stop of 2026-09-02 carries `tank_percent_before: 44.0` and `tank_percent_after: 74.0`. The rule that selects between them says only:

> "…counted as the programme's fill-to percentage of the tank's water capacity less **the gauge reading the driver recorded at the most recent stop**, taken on that capacity and rounded to one decimal place"

and that sentence is **identical, word for word, in the source-layer factor ladder (`energy_ext_protection_floor_credit.factors[undrawn_holdback_basis].ladder[0].method`) and in the published document** `gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json`. Neither names a column. The choice is made only in the source's `compute` binding, which is not renderable:

> `last_gauge_after: "float(LATEST('energy_deliveries','tank_percent_after', …) or 0)"`

So the ambiguity **originates on the policy side**: the rule sentence does not entail which of the two recorded readings it means, and the KB is a faithful, verbatim carriage of it. The documents are not the source of the divergence; the rule sentence is.

**Aggravating document-side factor.** The rendered document supplies an illustration that the source does not have, and its chosen figure reads naturally as the arrival gauge rather than the after-fill gauge:

> `gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json`, "Worked illustrations": *"A tank of 1000.0 gallons water capacity stands on the automatic keep-full schedule on a programme whose fill-to percentage is 80 percent, and 5 stops were made on the account in the twelve months ending on the handling date. **The driver's gauge reading at the most recent stop was 35 percent.** The held-back gallons are 80 percent less 35 percent of 1000.0 gallons, coming to 450.0 gallons."*

35 percent is below the programme's fill-to of 80 percent, which the same document's opening explains the fill runs to; and the document's stated rationale — *"part of the gallons standing to the member's credit is spoken for by **the fill the schedule will make next**"* — describes a quantity measured from where the tank stands, not from where a completed fill left it. On a keep-full stop the after-fill reading is the fill-to by construction, which would make the tier's subtraction zero. All three of these push a careful reader to the arrival column. Because the source leaves the boundary open, the corpus should not close it either; this illustration closes it, and closes it away from the scored reading.

**Evidence.**
- Query return, `find_energy_deliveries {"energy_account_id": "c2cc7c02-3bc6-4b9e-b756-621e05087059"}`: `{'event_type': 'energy_delivery_made', 'ticket_number': 'ET-6613655', 'delivery_date': '2026-09-02', 'delivery_type': 'will_call', 'gallons': 300.0, 'tank_percent_before': 44.0, 'tank_percent_after': 74.0, …}`.
- Published document: `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/docs/energy/gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json`, table row 1 and the "Worked illustrations" paragraph.
- Source: `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/energy_delivery_desk/energy.extended.yaml`, `energy_ext_protection_floor_credit` → `compute[last_gauge_after]` and `factors[0].ladder[0].method`.
- Scored values: `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/0.json`, `computations[0].expected = 188.97`, `computations[2].expected = 3648.14`; `evaluation_criteria[7].arguments.gallons = 1240.0`.

**Affected documents and locations.** `docs/energy/gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json` (title/content: the first table row and the "Worked illustrations" section). Downstream consequence only, no defect of their own: `working_out_a_downside_protection_credit_777bb283.json` (quantity 1) and `arriving_at_the_amount_that_clears_an_account_48d31667.json` (amount standing).

**Not attributed to the solving agent.** The divergence is not an arithmetic slip: every other intermediate on the path (rack of record, margin, posted price, protected floor, prior offset, days overdue, chargeable months, arrears rate, late charge, settlement allowance, and the whole of the true-up) was reproduced to the cent from the visible materials.

**Nature, for the record.** This is a policy-side ambiguity that no gate can catch — `check_docs.py` proves the ladder is carried verbatim (which it is) and `check_traceability.py` proves gold arguments are copyable (they are), and neither compares the rule's prose against the binding its `compute` chooses. The faithful side is the policy; the remedy belongs there, at the rule sentence, not in the document. This audit names the semantics the visible materials fail to fix — which of the two driver-recorded gauge readings a stop's reading is — and stops there.

and the binding moved with it: `last_gauge_before: float(LATEST('energy_deliveries','tank_percent_before', …) or 0)`. The sentence now names one of the two recorded readings and excludes the other by its own words, so it entails a single number.
